messages:
Amal: Taking over the night shift now. Seeing an active P1 (503s + token latency) on prod-west1. Paging history shows spikes started ~10m ago. Can someone pick driver and comms? :rotating_light:

incident-bot: INCIDENT #1234 detected — service:redwood-api-prod (west1) — symptom: 5xx spike, latency > 2s, triggered at 1765432092. PagerDuty: paged oncall.

Kez: I can drive for the next 30m, I'm already at my desk. Amal — are you still available for quick handover notes? My overlap ends in ~20m.

Amal: Yup on my side. Quick summary: errors look concentrated on the runtime pod pool (serve-prod) and correlates with a KV cache miss flood from a new batch job. Link to quick playbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/runtime-503

Rowan: I'm in a standup for 10m, can’t be primary, but I can act as secondary and run the mitigation commands if you ask.

Tess: I can own external comms for 45m (can post status updates + customer DM'ing). Please give me short bullets I can paste.

Kez: OK I’ll drive. Plan: (1) confirm affected hosts, (2) scale up the dedicated pool by +2 nodes, (3) enable fallback routing to the smaller-model variant for latency-sensitive routes, (4) watch for error rate drop. Rowan — can you run the scale + routing commands once Amal and I confirm pods?

Amal: Commands to start with (from runbook):
```
# check runtime pods and restart-degraded replicas
kubectl -n rwd get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
# tail recent errors
kubectl -n rwd logs deploy/serve-prod -c runtime --since=15m | tail -n 150
# scale dedicated pool (internal allocator)
rwdctl infra scale --pool serve-prod-dedicated --add 2
# set routing fallback for low-latency paths (temporary)
rwdctl route set --policy fallback=cheap-variant --scope=prod-west1 --ttl=30m
```

Rowan: Running `kubectl get pods` now. Seeing 3 pods in CrashLoopBackoff and high OOM lines in logs — looks like the KV cache is blowing memory on a subset of requests. I'll join the pod restart and then trigger scale if restarts don't stabilize.

Kez: I'll open a quick checkpoint in PagerDuty notes and tag #customers-affected. Tess, here's a comms draft: 
- Short status: "We're investigating elevated errors impacting inference in west1. We've routed traffic to a lower-latency model variant and are scaling capacity. We'll post updates every 20 minutes"
- Impact: "Some requests may see 5xx or elevated latency; embeddings and batch jobs likely impacted first."
- Next update ETA: 20m

Tess: Copy. I'll post the first update in 5m and handle any inbound customer threads. Please DM me if anything changes.

Amal: If scaling doesn't restore stability within 8-10m, follow runbook mitigation step: flush KV prefix cache for the suspected job (coord with the batch owner). Command: `rwdctl cache flush --prefix job/ingest-2026-03 --confirm` — do this only after thumbs-up from batch owner or if OOM persists after restart.

Kez: Noted. I'm watching metrics now. Error rate down ~15% after restarting two pods but still above threshold. Rowan — did the scale command start?

Rowan: Kicked off `rwdctl infra scale` and it's provisioning two additional GPUs (ETA ~4m). Also opened a ticket with the batch team to pause the job causing KV pressure.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note added: "Kez is primary driver; Tess is comms owner; Rowan secondary/infra".

Amal: Handing off final for overlap — Kez driving, Tess comms, Rowan infra backups. If anything escalates to tenant-impacting or >30m, escalate to the senior oncall (page: @director-oncall).

Kez: Acknowledged. I'll keep the thread updated. First public update queued by Tess at +5m.

Tess: Posted update: https://status.redwood/notice/1234 — ping me for copy edits.

Kez: Quick checklist for whoever picks up next shift: 
- Confirm `serve-prod` pod stability (no CrashLoopBackoff)
- Confirm routing policy reverted when healthy (rwdctl route unset or set ttl expiry)
- Confirm batch job either paused or KV prefix flushed if it caused OOMs
- Add notes to incident page: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1234

Amal: Thanks team — I'll be on-call slack for another 10m if anything pops. Good handover.

Rowan: Scale complete, nodes healthy. Error rate trending down. Leaving secondary watch.

Kez: Closing this update for now. Last check-in at 1765432280 — handing off to night crew lead when they join.

Tess: All good — comms owner handing off in next update. Will paste the final debrief. :white_check_mark:
